newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude gets help from arb, thin programme.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude gets help from arb, thin programme.

text.p: North Sea wet crude was steady to a shade firmer on Friday, drawing support from an attractive transatlantic arbitrage and thin supply in June, traders said.
Dated Brent was steady at around July Brent -20/-15 cents amid talk that several late May cargoes were offered into the U.S. Gulf on Thursday.
"The arb looks wide open at the moment," said a major North Sea producer.
Brent CFDs edged higher, with unconfirmed talk of May 19-23 changing hands at July Brent -23 cents and May 27-30 at July Brent -21 cents, a cent or two firmer than on Thursday.
Only two Brent cargoes, the first from the June loading programme, were due to turn wet on Friday, traders said.
Cash July Brent shed four cents to $19.45 a barrel and intermonth spreads were a shade easier, slipping five cents to trade at flat for June/July.

But the prospect of thinner North Sea loadings -- expected to fall by about 12.50 million barrels in the shorter month of June due to maintenance programmes -- was boosting other grades despite a small end May overhang.
A June 8-10 Oseberg traded late Thursday at Dated Brent +15 cents, 25 cents higher than a deal for a May cargo the same day.
"The prompt cargoes are certainly going for a lot less but on the Oseberg programme there is nothing scheduled in the June 9-14 period," said a trader.
"It's going to be pretty tight next month."
A couple of May Osebergs and three Ekofisks remained unsold, traders said.
In the Mediterranean, no deals were reported early Friday but traders said a refiner swapped an early June Russian Urals for a May 20-24 loader from an independent trader on Thursday.
